entries.desc: A single regression run executes the same plan serially and in parallel and prints serial, parallel and speedup numbers measured on the same host

evidence.note: integration_test (kind corrected from manual_transcript; pin, selector and assertions unchanged). The pinned command is an integration test: it drives the real executeValidationPlan and spawns real node child processes, and marker B7DFF-CHK004-MEASURED-MAKESPAN asserts one run measured the SAME plan at jobs=1 and jobs=4 and printed the serial / parallel / speedup numbers it observed, with the only threshold being the serial makespan measured moments earlier on the same host (no speedup constant is encoded). That gate-enforced regression measures a SYNTHETIC 6-command fixture by design, because it is itself registered in validate.commands. The REAL-plan number is now measured by a separate, repeatable, ON-DEMAND command added for F-002: npm run bench:validate-parallel (packages/main/src/tasks/validate-parallel-benchmark.ts), marker B7DFF-BENCH-REAL-PLAN-MEASURED. It reads the plan through the same configuredValidationCommands reader the validate handler uses and runs it twice through the real executeValidationPlan with jobs passed explicitly. Measured once on the final tree 3c4413ce0a (clean, dirtyFiles=0), order=parallel-first, at commands=107 declared=97 exclusiveByDefault=10: jobs=1 = 2225.0s, jobs=4 = 1474.9s, speedup = 1.51x. Both modes reported 106 passed / 1 failed and ZERO per-command verdict disagreement. The single failure is validate.commands[6] (review-pass-discard-smoke) timing out at its own 180000ms budget in BOTH modes -- it passes standalone in 177s on an idle host, so it is a marginal per-command budget under load, not a parallelism effect. The makespan is dominated by validate.commands[37] (quorum-submit-smoke) at 684s under jobs=4 and 752s under jobs=1, i.e. one command is about 46 percent of the parallel makespan, which structurally caps the achievable speedup. HONESTY: 1.51x sits at the BOTTOM of the 1.5-1.7x band this story has been quoting, and it is ONE sample per mode on a loaded host that has previously shown roughly 28 percent spread between identical full-plan runs (781.3s vs 611.6s); the benchmark prints that caveat itself. The benchmark is deliberately NOT registered in lattice.config.json validate.commands (it would make validate recursive and cost tens of minutes) and produces NO gate evidence -- the real-plan number is repeatable on demand, not gate-enforced.

entries.desc: Declaring a claim for a command that actually writes a repo-shared path is caught by a collision probe that fails, instead of the run merely appearing faster

evidence.note: The probe is given a synthetic plan in which one audited repo-shared writer (red-1734-reader-race, which renames the repository packages/main/dist and takes the real build lock) HAS been given the shared claim, and it must report exactly that command together with the reason the audit refused it. Synthetic input on purpose: mutating the real config to prove this would be the repo-shared write the audit is about. Independently confirmed against the real config too: flipping red-1734-reader-race to declared in lattice.config.json made the test exit 1 with AssertionError naming it, and the file was restored. Separately, the first full validate run of this change (871s) exited fail because red-b49d4-registration-derivation caught an uncommitted lattice.config.json, showing a repo-shared write inside this plan surfaces as a failure rather than a silently faster run.
